name: Utah
sources: 2026 S.B. 60: rate cut from 4.5% to 4.45%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (house.utleg.gov/taxes; EY Tax News 2026-1045)

Utah Code 59-10-1018 (taxpayer tax credit) as amended by 2026 H.B. 77: 6% of federal standard deduction (or itemized less state income tax) plus 6% of the personal exemption, reduced by 1.3% of Utah taxable income above the base amount
Utah TC-40 2025 (files.tax.utah.gov/tax/forms/current/tc-40.pdf), lines 10-20: $2,111 personal exemption per dependent, 6% credit, 1.3% phase-out

Utah Pub 14 withholding, effective June 2026 (via USDA NFC bulletin help.nfc.usda.gov/bulletins/2026/1782763921.htm): exempt wages $9,348 single / $18,696 married, used to derive the 2026 base amounts
Credit per filer = 6% x 2026 federal standard deduction $16,100 (src/data/2026/federal.json); per senior = 6% x $1,650 federal 65+ add-on
provisional: Credit phase-out base amounts ($18,696 single/MFS, $37,392 joint, $28,045 head of household) are derived from the Tax Commission's June 2026 withholding tables; the 2026 TC-40 is not yet published.
The dependent exemption inside the credit ($2,111, so $126.66 of credit per dependent) is the 2025 amount; the 2026 indexed amount is not yet published.
The 65+ part of the credit uses the married federal add-on ($1,650 x 6% = $99); unmarried filers actually get 6% of $2,050 ($123).
notes: Utah's taxpayer credit is figured on the single-filer federal standard deduction; head-of-household filers and those who itemize federally may owe up to about $500 less.
Utah's child tax credit and its retirement and Social Security credits are not included.
